sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Jǫrð** ​(*jord*) — ‌Earth, ‌Mother ​of Thor ​· ​Earth — ​belongs ​to ‌the Norse ​tradition, ​where ‌it is ​catalogued ‌under the ​domain ‌"Earth, ​Mother of ​Thor". ​The name ​means ​"Earth"[^1].

‌**Jǫrð** belongs ​to ‌the ​Norse tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌associated ​with ‌earth, mother ​of ​thor.[^2]

PuniCodex ‌restores ‌the ‌name as ​**Jǫrð** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at [jord.com](https://punicodex.com/jord/). ‌The ​restoration ​preserves at ‌least ​one distinctive ‌feature ​— ​a diacritic ​or ​a distinctive ‌letter ‌— ​that the ‌ASCII ​form ​loses, and ‌exactly ‌one historically ‌valid ‌Unicode ​restoration exists, ‌which ​places the ​name ​in ‌Tier 1. ​The ​plain ​ASCII form ‌*jord* ​survives as ​a ​modern ‌convenience imposed ​by ‌the early ​domain-name ‌system; ​the restoration, ‌not ‌the ​fallback, is ​the ​form the ​project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation survives ‌for this ​name; **Jǫrð** ​is a ​scholarly transliteration ​of the ​reconstructed spoken ‌form. Etymologically ​the name ​means "Earth"[^1].

‌The reconstructed ​proto-form is ‌*erþō* (proto-germanic, ​"earth"). ‌Old Norse ​Jǫrð, from ​Proto-Germanic *erþō ​'earth'; personified ​as a ​jötunn and ‌mother of ​Thor by ‌Odin.

The ​ASCII form ‌*jord* survives ​only because ‌the early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not carry ​diacritics; it ‌is a ‌technological compromise, ‌not an ​ancient spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration **Jǫrð** ​recovers the ​full diacritic ‌detail of ​the scholarly ​transliteration directly ‌in ​the address ‌bar. The ​restoration preserves ​at least ​one distinctive ​feature — ‌a diacritic ‌or a ​distinctive letter ‌— that ​the ASCII ​form loses, ‌and exactly ‌one historically ‌valid ‌Unicode restoration ​exists, which ‌places the ​name in ​Tier 1.

​The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- **j** ​→ **J** ​— Same, ‌capitalized
- ​**o** → ​**ǫ** — ​O ‌with ogonek: ​nasalized vowel
‌- **r** ​→ **r** ‌— Same
​- **d** ‌→ **ð** ‌— Eth: ​voiced dental ​fricative

The ​canonical temple ​for this ‌name is ‌served at ​**jord.com**[^2].

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/jord/** ​— ​Norse ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**J** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Jǫrð.
‌- ​**ǫrð** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Norse tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'JORD' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Norse** ​— Jǫrð, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Jǫrð ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Norse ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Jǫrð** ‌circulate within ​the ​Norse corpus, ​where the ​figure ​embodies earth, ‌mother ​of thor.[^1]

​### ‌Primary Attestation ​(Sources)

‌Jǫrð is ​attested ‌in the ​canonical Norse ​sources ​as a ​figure ​associated with ‌earth, ​mother of ‌thor.[^2]

​### Name ‌and ​Meaning (Etymology)

‌The name ​means ‌"Earth" and ​reflects ​the figure's ‌role ‌in the ‌tradition. ​**Jǫrð** is ​the ‌personified earth ​in Norse ​myth ‌and the ​mother ​of Thor ‌by ​Odin. Her ‌name ​is cognate ​with ​English "earth," ​and she ‌represents ‌the fertile ​ground ‌that receives ​the ​sky's rain.[^1] ‌Though ‌little is ‌said ‌of her ​directly, her ‌maternal ​bond to ​Thor ​makes her ‌one ​of the ​most ​consequential figures ‌in ​the pantheon. ​Snorri's *Gylfaginning* ​calls ‌her one ​of ‌Óðinn's wives ​and ‌a daughter ​of ‌Nótt and ‌Annarr, ​linking her ​to the ​generative ​night and ‌the ‌primordial giantess ​line.[^2]
